newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds see curve flattening, short end slips.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds see curve flattening, short end slips.

text.p: Irish government bonds were mixed in afternoon trade on Friday with the shorter end retreating on position-squaring ahead of the a holiday weekend and caution about Sunday's election in France, dealers said.

"We've seen some curve flattening, in reasonable volumes," one dealer said. "It's partly because of the holiday weekend and partly because of worries about the French elections -- worries about EMU (economic and monetary union) tend to hurt the short end in Dublin more than the long end."
Analysts said a victory for the left in France's election could increase the chances that EMU will be delayed.
By 1435 GMT the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was five pence weaker at 101.80 to yield 6.01 percent, while the eight percent benchmark bond due 2006 was 10p firmer at 108.60 to yield 6.71 percent.
Dealers said the shorter end of the curve had underperformed Germany, by around four basis points in the five-year area.
Monday is a holiday in Ireland and markets will be closed.
